m.title: Paper 2: Writing Code from a Scenario
m.q: Write an algorithm to input three integers and output their total.
st: Repeat three times to input a number.
Add each entered number to total.

idoVisual.title: I DO · Paper 2: Writing Code from a Scenario
idoVisual.topic: Paper 2: Writing Code from a Scenario
idoVisual.caption: Explain each part of the answer

w: Design a program to input five marks and count those ≥ 50.

wVisuals.title: WE DO · Paper 2: Writing Code from a Scenario
wVisuals.topic: Paper 2: Writing Code from a Scenario
wVisuals.caption: Explain each part of the answer

k.code:
total = 0
for i = 1 to 3
    total = total + 2
next i
print(total)
p: Explain the first assignment or condition that determines the output.
Extend to input one value on each pass instead of adding 2.
k.a: 6; 10; use an input statement and total=total+value.

e: Write OCR-style pseudocode to output the larger of two input values. [4 marks]
Input a,b; if a>b print(a), else print(b); equality may output either as both are largest.
Explain why an accumulator starts at zero when summing values. [2 marks]
Zero is the additive identity and avoids introducing an unwanted starting total.
State why a final output statement should be outside a loop when only one total is required. [2 marks]
Inside the loop would print intermediate totals repeatedly.
v: List all inputs, types and relevant constraints before writing code.
State algorithm steps separately from program syntax.
Write appropriate IF/ELSE and loops rather than unnecessary repetition.
Check both a typical value and at least one boundary/unexpected condition.
x: The same program line must be copied five times instead of using a loop.
r: A linear search seeks 7 in [3,5,7,9]. Give number of checks.
Explain why encryption protects intercepted information.
The interceptor sees ciphertext; without the relevant key it is not readily readable.
State why a program should be tested after fixing an IDE-reported syntax error.
Syntax correction only ensures code can be parsed; logical behaviour still needs checking.

stretch.task: Modify the loop to accept a different value each pass and add them.
stretch.hint: Use input() inside the loop, not fixed +2.

mastery.task: Write a program that accepts marks until a sentinel -1, ignores invalid marks above100 and outputs count and average of valid marks only.
mastery.hint: Guard division by zero if no valid marks.
mastery.answer: For 50,150,70,-1: valid count2, total120, average60; 150 excluded; immediate -1 -> no average available.
